Figure 1:Examples of ViRA-Bench and ViRA-Bench-Real.Each set shows the original photo (O, cut to 16:9) with the object in a yellow box.
The insets show the object in O and the two variants (A, B), with the correct answers.
Below each set are the original’s answer and the number of baseline settings, out of 15 (AppendixD.1), that give this answer to all three versions at 1 MP.
Questions are shortened.

Figure 4:Where the agents lookon one contrast set of ViRA-Bench at 1 MP.
Each tile is the agent’s last crop, or the whole photo if it received no crop.
For the open models, colors show the attention of the final reply to each part of the tile, relative to a request for a general description of the image[82], so red marks where the reply looks more than usual.
AppendixH.2gives the details and 14 other sets.

Figure 7:Case study on ViRA-Bench at 1 MP: seven models on 14 sets (Figures7to10).A row shows one variant or all three versions of a set.
It gives the question, the whole photo with the object in a yellow box, the object at full resolution in each version, and for every model the last crop that it received with its answer.
A yellow box in a crop marks the object, and a model that received no crop of the photo is shown with the whole photo.
For the open models, colors show where the final reply looks in the shown image (AppendixH.2).
Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6-Luna run at max thinking.

Figure 8:Case study (continued).The layout is as in Figure7.
Baselines give the original’s answer on a variant, and both ViRA agents answer every shown version correctly.

Figure 9:Case study (continued).The layout is as in Figure7.
(a, b) The proprietary models have the object in their last crop but give the original’s answer.
(c, d) They zoom up to six times without covering the object.
(e) ViRA-9B gives this answer on every version.

Figure 10:Case study (continued).The layout is as in Figure7.
ViRA-9B zooms once and gives the original’s answer on the variants, whereas ViRA-27B zooms several times and answers correctly.
